CHIEF COMPLAINT
Runny nose, nasal congestion, cough, fever, and irritability

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presents with approximately 1 day history of upper respiratory symptoms that began around supper time yesterday evening. Per parent/guardian, patient developed a runny nose with clear nasal discharge and nasal congestion. Patient also has developed a non-barky cough and has been ear-pulling and rubbing at his nose. Parent documented low-grade fever with rectal temperature of 100.3°F. Appetite has decreased, with patient consuming approximately 7 ounces from bottle this morning, refusing offered cereal, and barely finishing a second bottle. Patient appears irritable but energetic, though parent notes difficulty with sleep and patient "fighting" sleep attempts. Patient has been exposed to older sister who is currently ill with similar symptoms. Additionally, patient had recent playdate with nephew who was subsequently found to have sinus infection. At-home treatments attempted include saline nasal mist, acetaminophen given early this morning for fever, baby Vick's applied to feet, and humidifier use overnight.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Constitutional: Fever (rectal temperature 100.3°F), decreased appetite, irritability
Head, Eyes, Ears, Nose, Throat: Rhinorrhea with clear discharge, nasal congestion, non-barky cough, otalgia (ear pulling), nasal rubbing
Sleep: Difficulty falling asleep, fighting sleep
Energy: Energetic but irritable

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Cradle cap (recently worsened)

MEDICATIONS
- Acetaminophen (Tylenol) - given once this morning for fever
- Saline nasal mist - in-home use
- Baby Vick's - applied to feet
- Aveno shampoo - for cradle cap

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Older sibling currently ill with similar upper respiratory symptoms; nephew with recent sinus infection

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recent playdate exposure to ill family member

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- General: Cooperative, energetic child
- Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally with excellent air movement
- Ears: Normal appearance, no acute findings
- Skin: Cradle cap noted with apparent worsening from baseline
- Rest of examination: Unremarkable

RESULTS
COVID-19: Negative
Clinical impression: Acute viral upper respiratory infection

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute viral upper respiratory infection
   - Currently appears viral in etiology without indication for antibiotics at this time
   - Continue supportive care with hydration and rest
   - Monitor closely for development of barky/croupy cough which would indicate need for intervention
   - Prescription provided for cough medicine to be used only if barky cough develops; if needed, administer 1/2 teaspoon for 5 days
   - For regular non-barky cough: Zarbee's may be used at dosing appropriate for children under 1 year of age
   - Counseled regarding honey: Avoid honey in children under 1 year due to botulism risk; agave may be used as alternative
   - Follow-up appointment scheduled for 1 week
   - Instructed to call if symptoms worsen prior to follow-up visit

2. Cradle cap management
   - Discontinue current non-medicated Aveno shampoo
   - Switch to medicated dandruff shampoo: Head & Shoulders, Selsun Blue, or Nizoral AD (regular strength only, not extra strength)
   - Continue use of soft cradle cap brush to gently remove dead scales
   - Apply baby oil to assist with scale removal
   - Use medicated shampoo twice weekly (approximately every 2-3 days); use regular shampoo on non-treatment days
   - Avoid contact with eyes during hair rinsing
   - Expected improvement within approximately 6 weeks
   - Contact office if condition worsens
